name: Sophia Lin
description: Research, essays, and performances by Sophia Lin.
intro: I am a Harvard sophomore studying computer science, statistics, and philosophy.
bio: At NIST, I study LLM judges and adversarial verification: whether evaluators measure what they claim to measure, and whether independent verifiers improve the factual grounding of AI systems.

projects.title: Characterizing LLM Judges as Measurement Instruments
projects.text: I led the design of a measurement framework testing entailment, claim reasoning and decomposition, error recognition, confidence, and abstention. More than 15 probes compare blind, correct-guidance, and deliberately false-guidance conditions to separate evaluation capability from prompt sensitivity and sycophancy.

projects.title: Adversarial Verification for Agentic AI Grounding
projects.text: I am designing controlled experiments to test whether independent verifier agents with competing objectives improve factual grounding. The evaluation tooling tests citation-grounded reasoning, deception, hallucination, contradiction handling, and reliance on retrieved evidence when it conflicts with parametric knowledge.

projects.title: Bayesian Modeling of Multi-Stage Censoring
projects.institution: RSI · MIT CSAIL · Harvard Medical School
projects.text: I co-developed a Bayesian model of sequential selection and censoring to recover latent patient risk from incomplete clinical decision pipelines and examine disparities in triage.

projects.title: FRISTS: Interpretable Time-Series Prediction
projects.text: I led development of an interpretable model that extracts temporal patterns from clinical records and produces human-auditable risk estimates. We developed and validated the method using 18 million longitudinal health records, outperforming prior heart-failure prediction baselines.

projects.title: Longitudinal Analysis of Federal ROTC Programs
projects.text: I built Python, R, and SAS pipelines integrating 30 years of enrollment, commissioning, funding, and program data, with edit checks and clustering analyses across inconsistent longitudinal records.
